reproducibility.claim: The carrier records Java 21, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.242, the 2101.x FTB compatibility policy, Gradle build tasks, GameTest source configuration, JAR audit, and runtime validation entry points.

A clean checkout of the exact carrier revision reproduced the build and bounded runtime validation workflow on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu. This supports a repeatable validation recipe, not byte-for-byte deterministic artifact reproduction.

interoperability.claim: The active carrier documents Minecraft/NeoForge and FTB Chunks compatibility boundaries and explicitly separates BuyClaimChunks personal capacity from FTB Public Claims public capacity and ownership.

The exact-head compatible-stack run exercised FTB Chunks 2101.1.21, FTB Teams 2101.1.10, FTB Library 2101.1.34, Architectury 13.0.8, NeoForge 21.1.242, and BuyClaimChunks Continued 1.1.1 together, including metadata-policy and client-ABI checks.

security-safety.claim: The carrier documents public-versus-personal ownership separation, non-overwrite behavior, public interaction policy, PvP/explosion/mob-grief/fake-player defaults, and a migration boundary that deliberately avoids auto-merging legacy claims when ownership could conflict.

Exact-head runtime validation exercised public claim/unclaim and interaction behavior together with BuyClaimChunks Continued and verified durable public state across a second JVM; this evidence is bounded to the tested ownership/protection/runtime contract and is not a general security audit.

stewardship.claim: The active carrier records its supported runtime range, exact verified dependency stack, compatibility-sensitive integration boundary, validation expectations, and conservative legacy-save migration policy.

The exact-head build includes a fail-closed distributable-JAR audit and runtime evidence spanning dependency ABI, client interaction, GameTests, and persistence. This supports bounded stewardship of the active carrier without claiming that the draft is a stable release.
